sections.title: Choosing the ending
sections.content: Most place words you know have a back vowel, so they take *-ban*: *iskola* becomes *iskolában*, *iroda* becomes *irodában*, *nappali* becomes *nappaliban*. In *nappali* the *i* is neutral, so the *a* decides. Words with only front vowels take *-ben*: *terem* becomes *teremben*, *kert* becomes *kertben*, *szekrény* becomes *szekrényben*.

sections.title: What happens at the end
sections.content: The final *-a* of *iskola* and *iroda* grows long (*á*). The final *-i* of *nappali* does not change.

items.english: The key is in the cupboard.
Anna is in the large room.

sections.content: Do not guess from the English word. Look at the vowels in the Hungarian word: *terem* has only *e*, so *-ben*; *iskola* has *o* and *a*, so *-ban*. And keep the accent on a lengthened vowel: *irodában* has *á*, and *irodaban* is a misspelling.
